- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment turns negative (≤ -1.0) or shows strong reversal, model often overshoots downward; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% to avoid premature drop.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 5% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +1/-1 patterns, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; apply slight upward bias if recent sentiment is negative, or downward if positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply 1–2% downward adjustment to first 5 days of forecast.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.0), model tends to err on the high side; reduce forecast by 1–2% to align with true mean.
